fixes.was: Mr Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi, whose Slough constituency has significant data-centre development, asked whether government had considered water and energy impact assessments for data centres, what assessment had been made of the impact of multiple data-centre developments on local water, temperature, biodiversity and electricity demand, and how compliance with the Data Centre Covenant's community-benefit requirements will be monitored and enforced. Ministers pointed to the Written Ministerial Statement on "Enabling Sustainable Data Centre Growth Through Responsible Water and Energy Use", which requires strategic data centres to report annually on water and energy use, and said operators are encouraged to meet Data Centre Covenant tests.
fixes.now: Mr Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi, MP for Slough, asked about water and energy impact assessments, the local water, temperature, biodiversity and electricity impacts of multiple data-centre developments, and monitoring and enforcement of the Data Centre Covenant's community-benefit requirements. In answers to UINs 43026 and 43027, Martin McCluskey referred to the Written Ministerial Statement on "Enabling Sustainable Data Centre Growth Through Responsible Water and Energy Use". He said strategic data centres will have to report annually on water and energy use, efficiency, emissions and heat reuse. All new data centres are encouraged to meet Covenant tests; strategically important centres seeking enhanced government support will be required to meet them. No answer to the community-benefit enforcement question, UIN 45176, is recorded.
fixes.reason: Slough's supposed scale of data-centre development is not evidenced. Distinguish answered environmental questions from the unanswered enforcement question, and voluntary Covenant tests from the specified mandatory category.

fixes.was: Rupert Lowe asked whether government would introduce a statutory right to a free non-digital alternative for identity verification; Sorcha Eastwood asked whether onboarding of further services onto GOV.UK One Login would be paused pending independent review, with a statutory guarantee of non-digital alternatives. The government said One Login is not mandatory, alternative routes remain available, and the rollout will continue, overseen by HM Treasury, NISTA and the UK Digital Verification Services Trust Framework.
fixes.now: Rupert Lowe asked about the merits of a statutory right to a free non-digital alternative for identity verification. Sorcha Eastwood asked whether additional GOV.UK One Login onboarding would be paused pending independent review and whether free, genuinely equivalent non-digital alternatives would receive a statutory guarantee. The government said One Login is not mandatory, alternative routes are decided by the relevant service, and rollout will continue. It described departmental controls, HM Treasury oversight, independent assurance by NISTA and independent assurance and certification under the UK Digital Verification Services Trust Framework.
fixes.reason: UIN 39385 asks about assessing merits. UIN 41767 distinguishes oversight, independent assurance and certification; a trust framework is not an oversight body.
